checkpointModel.weightRule: Weights are positive integers declared once per slice and sum to 100. They come from the slice's declared scope, never from an estimate of effort.
checkpointModel.evidenceRule: A completed checkpoint names evidence. A blocked checkpoint names a blocker. A skipped checkpoint names a reason. A completed checkpoint without evidence is rejected by the validator.
checkpointModel.progressRule: The generator sums the weights of completed checkpoints. Status and progress are two axes. A blocked checkpoint keeps the points already earned and never resets progress to 0.
checkpointModel.timestampRule: A slice that declares checkpoints records updatedAt (ISO-8601 Z) and may record latestUpdate, so the register alone answers how fresh the state is.

checkpoints.title: Predictive admission controller (full): telemetry surface, bounded prediction, hysteresis, and the adapt_limits clamp repair
checkpoints.purpose: Observe latency, queue depth, CPU/memory pressure, admission rate, completion rate, error rate and recent burst shape, and adjust ONLY per-route concurrency, per-workflow concurrency, queue budget, low-priority admission and defer threshold. checkpoints.title: DELETE /rest/service-principals/:id: revoke with a tombstone
checkpoints.purpose: Revoke a service principal keeping a tombstone, so the credential is later reported REVOKED rather than UNKNOWN and the audit row survives. Revoking an unknown or already revoked id is a silent no-op, as upstream /rest/api-keys does, so the response never confirms that an id exists.
checkpoints.evidence: apps/n8n-lego/test/service-principal-routes.test.mjs — 'revoke keeps a tombstone': after DELETE the credential authenticates as REVOKED rather than UNKNOWN (the tombstone is what makes the distinction), the record survives with revokedAt set and the audit row with it, an unknown or already revoked id is a silent no-op returning {success:false}, and a revoked principal leaves the redacted list without leaving the store. Merged in 0845c25f.

checkpoints.title: PATCH /rest/service-principals/:id: ownership transfer
checkpoints.purpose: Transfer a service principal to another accountable owner, which is the P5.7 debt item 'no ownership transfer for service principals'. The authority moves, the tenant does not, the receiving owner must be able to hold the principal's scopes, and both sides are audited.

checkpoints.purpose: Resolve the node class of a candidate and prove that no class claim buys authority by itself: an attestation promotes one step and no further, AI-generated code is custom whatever it declares, and an unclassifiable candidate is never promoted by what it says about itself.
checkpoints.evidence: classifyNode in src/lego/node-install.mjs; tests 'an attestation promotes community one step and no further', 'a local artifact is never promoted by an attestation', 'AI-generated code is custom whatever it declares about itself', 'a class claim outside the vocabulary is refused, not coerced'.

checkpoints.title: Trust ceiling/floor resolution for every named class
checkpoints.purpose: Map every class issue #95 names to both a ceiling and a floor, so official reaches CORE's ceiling without ever being granted CORE, and no class can be placed outside the band its own class permits.
checkpoints.evidence: NODE_CLASS_TRUST_CEILING / NODE_CLASS_TRUST_FLOOR and resolveTrustClass; test 'every class has both a ceiling and a floor' asserts floor index >= ceiling index for all six classes.

checkpoints.title: Locality: the capability can take the in-process row away
checkpoints.purpose: Resolve where a node runs from the stricter of its class ceiling and the capabilities it requested, so an official node asking for subprocess lands in an isolated process instead of being waved into the process on the strength of its class claim.
checkpoints.evidence: resolveInstallLocality with strictestPosture; tests 'a native capability takes the in-process row away, whatever the class claims' and 'an official node requesting a native capability is downgraded to ISOLATED'.

checkpoints.title: Fail-closed three-way verdict (refuse / incomplete / admit)
checkpoints.purpose: Keep the three verdicts deliberately distinct: refuse means something failed, incomplete means nobody checked, admit means both are answered. Conflating a missing check with a failed check is the bug that produces 'tests mostly pass'.
checkpoints.evidence: installNode verdict derivation; tests 'a missing self-test is incomplete, not refuse' (caught a real inverted-verdict bug), 'a failed self-test is refused', 'a node over its resource budget is refused with the budget named'.

checkpoints.title: Consumer-contract stability under re-placement
checkpoints.purpose: Prove that moving a node behind a different runtime does not change the node a workflow sees: the install decision carries consumerContract { type } and nothing else, and the decision carries no grant of any kind.
checkpoints.evidence: Tests 're-placing a node does not change its consumer-facing contract' (in-process vs isolated, identical consumerContract) and 'the install decision never carries a grant, only a ceiling' (asserts no grants key exists).

checkpoints.title: DEC-0015 required self-hosted runner verification
checkpoints.purpose: Derive the DEC-0015 verdict for the delivery PR from the required self-hosted runner jobs, with real run IDs and real runner identities read from the jobs API, never simulated.
checkpoints.evidence: DEC-0015 verdict derived from the PR head check-runs and the actions/runs jobs API at merge time; recorded in the delivery PR body and in the register mergeSha reconciliation.

slices.title: Production WASM node/plugin sandbox engine (P6.26 compilation cache and P2.27.4 locality are the foundation)

checkpoints.title: Deny-by-default imports, no wildcards, refused rows never dropped
checkpoints.purpose: Prove the import table is the whole security boundary: an ungranted import is refused at instantiation rather than trapped later, a wildcard is refused rather than interpreted, and a refused row is never silently dropped from the resolution.
checkpoints.evidence: resolveImports / instantiate in src/lego/wasm-sandbox.mjs; tests 'an ungranted import is refused at instantiation, not trapped later', 'a refused row is never dropped from the resolution', 'a wildcard grant is refused, not interpreted' (covers '*', 'log.*', '*.log').

checkpoints.title: No ambient authority: every ambient capability is a withholdable import
checkpoints.purpose: Prove clock, random, filesystem, network, process and env are imports like any other, so a sandbox with no grants cannot reach them structurally, and that the ambient authorities a sandbox holds are recorded rather than inferred.
checkpoints.evidence: AMBIENT_IMPORTS and the recorded `ambient` field; tests 'a sandbox with no grants holds no ambient authority', 'every ambient authority is an import, so every one can be withheld' (all six), 'the ambient authorities a sandbox holds are recorded, not inferred'.

checkpoints.title: Fuel is a hard budget; fuel-exhausted is not trapped
checkpoints.purpose: Keep the four call outcomes distinct so an operator can tell a module that was stopped from a module that misbehaved, and make the budget override whatever the caller reported while keeping the ceiling inclusive.
checkpoints.evidence: accountCall; tests 'a call over its budget is stopped, and stopped is not completed', 'fuel-exhausted and trapped are different facts', 'using the whole budget is allowed: the ceiling is inclusive', 'a budget above the ceiling is refused rather than clamped'.

checkpoints.title: The sandbox never changes the consumer-facing node contract
checkpoints.purpose: Prove a node running behind the engine presents the same type identity as the same node in-process, with the locality recorded next to the node rather than inside it — P6-S01's rule, inherited not restated.
checkpoints.evidence: consumerContract on the instantiation decision; test 'the sandbox never changes the consumer-facing node contract' asserts deepEqual consumerContract and locality WASM alongside it.

checkpoints.title: P6.26 composition with the dependency inverted, hit verified before it runs
checkpoints.purpose: Prove a module is never run unless the cache entry verifies, that a cached compilation failure has no module to run, and that the lego-foundation -> node-registry boundary is respected by reading the entry as data instead of importing the cache module.
checkpoints.evidence: admitFromCache reads { outcome, moduleDigest } as data; tests 'a module is admitted from the cache only when the hit verifies', 'a module whose digest does not match the entry is never run', 'a cached compilation failure has no module to run and is refused' (asserts lookup state 'negative', the real P6.26 state), 'the engine reads the cache but never writes one'. lego:arch green after the inversion.

programs.title: Dynamic Parameters / Schema Runtime
programs.scope: Dynamic parameter schemas, option discovery, schema validation, caching, provider-backed lookup, parameter plugin boundaries (#90, #223).

slices.title: Parameter Contract & Compiler: canonical n8n parameter definitions compiled once into an immutable ParameterPlan with stable parameter identity and plan versioning (#223 §4-6, §31, §42 P7.1)
Visibility & Dependency Graph: displayOptions visibility engine, parameter dependency graph, incremental recomputation of only affected fields, expression boundary (#223 §7-10, §42 P7.2)

Local Validation & Normalization: schema validation, normalization, failure vocabulary and the immutable execution-ready parameter snapshot with canonical vs derived representation (#223 §20-21, §27, §29-30, §42 P7.3)

checkpoints.title: Canonical value model & normalization semantics: raw -> canonicalization -> type normalization -> canonical value, explicit and testable, no heuristic normalization that changes observable n8n behavior (#223 §21)
checkpoints.purpose: One deterministic normalization per parameter kind (string/number/boolean/options/collection/fixedCollection/resourceLocator) with explicit, documented, testable semantics that preserve observable n8n behavior.
checkpoints.evidence: normalizeValue performs only the two safe canonicalizations (finite numeric string -> number, 'true'/'false' -> boolean); every other value passes through unchanged, so observable n8n behavior is preserved (#223 §21). Pinned by the 4 normalization tests in test/lego-parameter-validate.test.mjs. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S03-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Schema validation vocabulary + structured errors: type/required/enum/pattern/min-max/length/array bounds/object rules/dependent requirement/normalized-value constraints; errors carry path, code, expected vs actual class, never secret material (#223 §20)
checkpoints.purpose: A compact canonical validation vocabulary over the compiled plan's extracted rules; structured, path-scoped errors with expected/actual classes and no secret leakage.
checkpoints.evidence: validateValue/applyRules + TYPE_OK implement the compact §20 vocabulary (type, required, enum, min/max, length, regex, email, minRequiredFields). Every issue is structured {path, code, rule, expected, actual, message} and never embeds the raw value (length-only / class-only). Absent values are a required problem, never a type problem. Pinned by 10 unit tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S03-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Failure vocabulary: SCHEMA_INVALID / DEPENDENCY_INVALID (local stage) with the full §27 set defined; validation failure is never converted into a fake empty success (#223 §27)
checkpoints.purpose: A closed, typed failure vocabulary for the local stage that distinguishes schema-invalid from dependency-invalid and never fabricates an empty success.
checkpoints.evidence: FAILURE_CODES is the closed §27 set (11 codes, frozen); LOCAL_FAILURE_CODES = [SCHEMA_INVALID, DEPENDENCY_INVALID] are the only codes this local stage emits. A validation failure keeps the actual values in normalized (never a fake empty success). Pinned by 3 unit tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S03-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Immutable execution-ready parameter snapshot: schema version, normalized values, unresolved expression refs where allowed, validation status, dependency digest; canonical vs derived, always reconstructible (#223 §29-30)
checkpoints.purpose: A compact deep-frozen execution snapshot derived from the plan + normalized values, clearly separated from the canonical workflow definition and reconstructible.
checkpoints.evidence: buildExecutionSnapshot/reconstructSnapshot produce the compact immutable §29 snapshot: deep-frozen, with schemaVersion, normalized values, unresolvedExpressions, validationStatus, issueCount and a dependencyDigest (SHA-256 over the canonical normalized values). It is §30-derived (never the canonical workflow definition) and reconstructible; re-derivation is byte-identical and the input is never rewritten or frozen. Pinned by 4 unit tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S03-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Negative/security matrix & determinism: malformed/oversized/missing inputs, circular/invalid dependencies, sensitive-value handling; idempotent, pure, no side effects (#223 §41, §44)
checkpoints.purpose: The local validation/normalization is a pure, idempotent, bounded local operation that fails safely on malformed input and never leaks sensitive values.
checkpoints.evidence: The stage is pure and deterministic: idempotent (two calls -> identical normalized values and digest), the input is never mutated or frozen, absent/missing containers fail safely (no throw, no false success), oversized forms are bounded (changed capped at 4096), and sensitive (password) values are validated by shape only and never echoed into issues. Pinned by 4 unit tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S03-EVIDENCE.md.

slices.title: Dynamic Options Runtime: /rest/dynamic-node-parameters options, bounded dynamic cache classes with stale-while-revalidate, dependent-field race protection, request coalescing, provider backpressure and resource budgets (#223 §11, §14-16, §23-26, §34, §42 P7.4)

checkpoints.title: Dynamic options resolution flow: parameter -> loadOptionsMethod -> resolved dependency context -> provider operation -> normalized option list; provider results normalized to the canonical shape (name, value, optional description); malformed provider data rejected, never passed to UI (#223 §11)
checkpoints.purpose: A deterministic resolution flow over an explicit, replaceable provider abstraction that normalizes provider results into a small canonical shape and rejects malformed data.
checkpoints.evidence: cacheKey composes nodeType + nodeVersion + parameterPath + methodName + normalizedDependencyDigest (SHA-256 over the canonical dependency context) + normalizedSearchQuery + providerVersion + schemaVersion, so distinct dependency contexts yield distinct keys and a digest change invalidates stale entries. Pinned by the cache-key tests in test/lego-parameter-discover.test.mjs. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S04-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Bounded dynamic cache + cache classes: cache key (nodeType + nodeVersion + parameterPath + methodName + normalizedDependencyDigest + searchQuery + providerVersion), bounded entries, STATIC/SESSION/REQUEST/PROVIDER/NEGATIVE classes; never caches credentials or secrets (#223 §14-15)
checkpoints.purpose: A bounded, keyed, classed cache that stores only normalized options + bounded metadata, with per-class TTL/eviction and no secret material.
checkpoints.evidence: DynamicCache is a bounded LRU with the STATIC/SESSION/REQUEST/PROVIDER/NEGATIVE classes (CACHE_CLASSES) and a per-class TTL; it stores only the normalized option list (never raw provider output or credentials), evicts by LRU at the bound, and peek/get/delete keep the SWR logic correct (#223 §14-15). Pinned by the cache-class/TTL/bound tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S04-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Stale-while-revalidate: display-only metadata may serve stale; security-sensitive / execution-authoritative values are revalidated before execution; cached UI state is never permission authority (#223 §16)
checkpoints.purpose: A two-tier freshness policy that never lets a cached UI option become assumed authority.
checkpoints.evidence: Stale-while-revalidate is display-only: a non-authoritative resolution serves a stale PROVIDER value within staleWindowMs and triggers a coalesced background revalidation; an authoritative resolution never serves stale (always revalidates or misses). The revalidation is non-recursive (it goes through the bounded _fetchAndCache path, never re-entering the SWR branch) (#223 §16). Pinned by the SWR tests (stale-served + background-revalidated, authoritative-never-stale, no-recursion). See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S04-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Dependent-field race protection + request coalescing: requestId, generation/version, dependency digest; only a response matching the current generation updates state; identical concurrent requests share one in-flight operation (#223 §24-25)
checkpoints.purpose: Correctness under overlapping editor changes (stale response discarded) and dedup of identical concurrent lookups.
checkpoints.evidence: Race protection: each issued provider call bumps the generation (carried on the result, captured at issue time) so a stale older-generation response is distinguishable; a dependency-digest change is a distinct cache key (no cross-contamination); identical concurrent requests coalesce onto one in-flight op (shared promise, shared generation) (#223 §24-25). Pinned by the race/coalescing tests (generation ordering, digest-change-misses, concurrent-coalesce). See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S04-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Backpressure + resource budgets: concurrency bound, deadline, timeout, max page size, max result count, max response bytes, retry budget, cancellation, negative cache; one slow provider cannot consume the whole process budget (#223 §26, §34)
checkpoints.purpose: Bounded, degrading resolution that treats a slow/broken provider as a failure, not a process-level resource problem.
checkpoints.evidence: DISCOVER_LIMITS enforces maxConcurrency, timeoutMs, maxResultCount (results truncated), retryBudget=0 (a failing provider is not retried), negativeTtlMs (a failure is negatively cached to stop a retry storm), providerTtlMs, staleWindowMs. A failing/slow/overloaded provider returns a marked failure (error + code) with options:[] — never a fake unmarked empty success — and one slow provider cannot consume the whole budget (#223 §26, §34). Pinned by the limit/failure tests (timeout, overload, negative-cache, failure-marked, maxResult truncation). See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S04-EVIDENCE.md.

slices.title: Resource Locator & Search: resourceLocator modes, list search with pagination and search (#223 §12-13, §42 P7.5)

checkpoints.title: resourceLocator canonical model: the four modes (list/name/id/url) with an n8n-compatible stored value
checkpoints.purpose: Treat resourceLocator as first-class P7 semantics (#223 §12): parse a stored n8n { mode, value } into a canonical form, validate the mode is one of list/name/id/url, and normalize each mode's value (name/id as bounded strings, url as a validated URL, list as the selected option value). Stored workflow values remain n8n-compatible; unknown modes or malformed values are rejected, never silently coerced.
checkpoints.evidence: parseResourceLocator/normalizeLocatorValue implement the four LOCATOR_MODES (list/name/id/url) as a canonical frozen { mode, value }; stored n8n values remain compatible (extra fields such as cachable are ignored); unknown modes and malformed values are rejected (SCHEMA_INVALID / INVALID_URL), never silently coerced; url mode validates the URL; values are length-bounded. Pinned by the 6 CP-01 tests in test/lego-parameter-locator.test.mjs. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S05-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Bounded list search with deterministic ordering + query length limits
checkpoints.purpose: List mode performs a targeted search (#223 §13): the query is length-bounded, results are normalized and deterministically ordered (stable sort by value then name), and the result count is bounded. Prefers targeted search over downloading a full remote catalog; never performs unbounded enumeration to populate a dropdown. Malformed provider data is rejected (INVALID_PROVIDER_DATA), never passed downstream.
checkpoints.evidence: ResourceLocatorSession.search performs a bounded targeted search: the query is length-bounded (maxQueryLength), results are normalized and deterministically ordered (sorted by value then name, independent of provider order), and the result count is bounded by maxPageSize/maxResultCount; a query returns only matching items (targeted, not the full catalog); a malformed provider page is rejected (INVALID_PROVIDER_DATA). Pinned by the 6 CP-02 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S05-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Bounded pagination: page size, next-page token, pages-per-session cap
checkpoints.purpose: Pagination is bounded (#223 §13): the page size is capped, each page carries a next-page token (opaque, length-bounded), and a per-session page cap stops unbounded enumeration. A page token that does not match the session/query is rejected (STALE_REQUEST). The session cannot walk the entire catalog.
checkpoints.evidence: Pagination is bounded: an opaque next-page token (length-bounded; a missing/overlong token is a marked STALE_REQUEST), pages walk the list without duplicates until exhausted, and the maxPagesPerSession cap stops unbounded enumeration (hitting the cap is a marked OVERLOADED, never a silent empty page). Pinned by the 3 CP-03 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S05-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Race protection, request coalescing, and cancellation
checkpoints.purpose: Every search gets a requestId + generation + normalized query digest (#223 §24): only a response matching the current generation updates state. Identical concurrent searches (same key + generation) coalesce onto one in-flight op (§25). Cancellation is supported (§26): a cancelled search is reported as a marked CANCELLED failure, and in-flight state is bounded and evicted.
checkpoints.evidence: Race protection: each issued provider call bumps the generation (carried on the result; distinct across searches). Coalescing: identical concurrent searches (same page key) share one in-flight op (the coalesced result is marked cache:'coalesced'). Cancellation: createCancelToken or session.cancel(requestId) reports a marked CANCELLED (the result is discarded; the provider was called once). Pinned by the 4 CP-04 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S05-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Failure vocabulary + resource budgets (no fake empty success)
checkpoints.purpose: A failing/slow/cancelled provider is reported with a closed, marked failure code (UNAVAILABLE/TIMEOUT/RATE_LIMITED/INVALID_PROVIDER_DATA/CANCELLED/STALE_REQUEST) — never converted into a fake unmarked empty success (#223 §27). Resource budgets reuse the P7-S04/§26/§34 primitives (concurrency bound, timeout, max response bytes, max result count); one slow provider cannot consume the whole process budget.
checkpoints.evidence: A failing/slow/cancelled provider returns items:[] TOGETHER with a non-null error (closed LOCATOR_FAILURE_CODES: UNAVAILABLE/TIMEOUT/RATE_LIMITED/OVERLOADED/CANCELLED/STALE_REQUEST, ...) — never a fake unmarked empty success; a genuine empty provider result is a success (error undefined). The concurrency bound is a marked OVERLOADED (one slow provider cannot consume the budget); failures are negatively cached to stop retry storms. Pinned by the 6 CP-05 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S05-EVIDENCE.md.

slices.title: Credential-Aware Resolution: credential/security composition through scoped SecretRefs and security-sensitive dynamic values that never leak into caches, snapshots or logs (#223 §18, §28, §42 P7.6)

checkpoints.title: Scoped SecretRef: a request-bound, opaque credential reference that never holds plaintext
checkpoints.purpose: A SecretRef is the only handle a dynamic lookup may carry for a credential (#223 §18): a request-bound, opaque reference bound to a capability scope (principal, tenant, capability, action, resource) + credentialId + nonce. It must NEVER contain raw credential material — passing plaintext (secret/password/token/value fields) is rejected (CREDENTIAL_LEAK). The SecretRef is immutable and safe to log (only its scope fields).
checkpoints.evidence: createSecretRef builds a request-bound, opaque, immutable SecretRef (credentialId + principal/tenant/capability/action/resource scope + nonce); it is the only credential handle a lookup may carry and REJECTS any plaintext field (secret/password/token/accessToken/apiKey/value) with CREDENTIAL_LEAK; a missing/empty scope field is rejected with INVALID_SECRET_REF. The ref is safe to log (scope fields only, never material). Pinned by the 3 CP-01 tests in test/lego-parameter-credential.test.mjs. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S06-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Credential composition pipeline: authorization -> SecretRef -> Secret Broker -> narrowly scoped provider operation -> normalized result
checkpoints.purpose: The §18 composition is modelled and enforced: an explicit, injectable Secret Broker (P2.27) resolves a SecretRef to in-memory credential material ONLY; a narrowly scoped provider operation receives the material in-memory and returns a normalized result. P7 never stores raw credential material — the material lives only for the duration of the operation and is never persisted, cached, or logged. The broker and provider are explicit, replaceable objects.
checkpoints.evidence: CredentialResolutionSession.resolve composes authorization -> SecretRef -> Secret Broker -> narrowly scoped provider operation -> normalized result (#223 §18): broker.resolve returns in-memory material (never persisted/logged), provider.invoke receives it, the result is normalized. A missing credential is a marked AUTH_REJECTED and the provider is never called; resolve() accepts only a SecretRef (raw material is rejected with INVALID_SECRET_REF). Pinned by the 3 CP-02 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S06-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Capability boundary: the principal -> tenant -> capability -> action -> resource -> SecretRef -> provider chain is enforced before the provider call
checkpoints.purpose: Before any provider call the full capability chain is checked (#223 §19) via an injectable P5 authorization decision. Option visibility does NOT grant permission to execute the resulting action (a visible option still requires the capability). Provider-returned metadata cannot grant itself new authority (authority-elevation fields in a provider result are ignored; the resolved authority is the original scope). A denied capability is a marked CAPABILITY_DENIED / AUTH_REJECTED and the provider is never called.
checkpoints.evidence: checkCapability enforces the principal -> tenant -> capability -> action -> resource -> SecretRef chain BEFORE the provider call via an injectable P5 decision (fail-closed: a missing authorizer or a denied decision is a marked CAPABILITY_DENIED and the provider is never called); option visibility does not grant permission to execute; the resolved authority is the original scope and provider-returned authority-elevation fields (grantedCapability/tenant) are ignored. Pinned by the 3 CP-03 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S06-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: No-leak guarantee: credential plaintext never appears in ParameterPlan, cache, parameter history, logs, telemetry, error payloads, or schema snapshots
checkpoints.purpose: The no-leak invariant (§18) is enforced structurally and by redaction: the cache key is over the SecretRef scope (never the material); the cache stores only the normalized result (never the material); a scrub() redactor strips any secret material from results, error payloads, and log/telemetry strings (a provider that echoes the credential back is scrubbed to [REDACTED]). Pinned by leak-detection tests: the material is absent from the cached value, the returned result, and any error message.
checkpoints.evidence: The no-leak invariant (#223 §18) is enforced structurally and by redaction: the cache key is over the SecretRef scope (never the material), the cache stores only the normalized result, and scrub/secretStrings redact any echoed material from the returned result AND error payloads (a provider that leaks the credential into a result description or an error message is scrubbed to [REDACTED]). Pinned by the leak-detection tests (the material is absent from the cache value, cache key, returned options, and error message). See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S06-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Security-sensitive dynamic values: authoritative values require revalidation; cached UI option never becomes authority
checkpoints.purpose: Security-sensitive / execution-authoritative values (valid resource IDs, allowed accounts, permission-bound resources) are marked revalidation-required (#223 §28): an informational option may use bounded stale metadata, but an authoritative resolution must revalidate against current authority before execution. The resolver never treats a cached UI option as authority — a cached option served for an authoritative request is refused (REVALIDATION_REQUIRED), preventing the cached-UI-option -> assumed-authority -> unauthorized-execution path.
checkpoints.evidence: Results are marked security: { sensitive: true, revalidationRequired: true } with the authoritative authority frozen to the original scope (#223 §28): an authoritative resolution drops the cache and always revalidates (never serves a cached UI option as authority — a second authoritative call re-invokes the provider), while a display resolution may serve a fresh cached result but remains revalidation-required. The closed CREDENTIAL_FAILURE_CODES set is frozen. Pinned by the 4 CP-05 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S06-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Provider registration/declaration boundary: identity, version, capability requirements, locality, trust class, budgets
checkpoints.purpose: A parameter provider may live inside a node/plugin, but registration must DECLARE (#223 §17, §33): provider identity, version, capability requirements, locality, runtime trust class, and resource budgets. registerProvider validates the declaration (rejecting incomplete/malformed ones) and normalizes it to the canonical descriptor — vendor-specific business-model fields are EXCLUDED from the public contract (P7 does not import vendor models into public parameter contracts). P6 owns node/runtime admission and trust; P7 owns parameter resolution (the trust class is declared and validated, not admitted, here).
checkpoints.evidence: registerProvider validates the full provider declaration (identity, version, capability requirements, locality, runtime trust class, resource budgets) and rejects incomplete/malformed ones (PROVIDER_DECLARATION_INVALID); it normalizes to a frozen canonical descriptor and EXCLUDES vendor-specific business-model fields from the public contract (P7 does not import vendor models). The trust class is validated (one of PROVIDER_TRUST_CLASSES) but admission/trust is P6's. Pinned by the 4 CP-01 tests in test/lego-parameter-provider-boundary.test.mjs. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S07-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Provider-backed schema: base schema + bounded provider fragment (versioned, size-bounded, validated, capability-scoped, cacheable, replaceable)
checkpoints.purpose: Support a base schema plus a bounded provider schema fragment (#223 §22). The fragment must be versioned, size-bounded, validated, capability-scoped, cacheable, and replaceable. A provider CANNOT replace the canonical P7 contract or security model: a fragment that attempts to override canonical/security fields (security/authorization/credentials/canonical) is rejected (SCHEMA_FRAGMENT_SECURITY_OVERRIDE). The base schema is always authoritative.
checkpoints.evidence: validateProviderSchemaFragment enforces that a provider schema fragment is versioned, size-bounded, validated, capability-scoped, cacheable, and replaceable; a fragment carrying a security/canonical override field (security/authorization/auth/credentials/canonical/permission/policy) is rejected (SCHEMA_FRAGMENT_SECURITY_OVERRIDE), and the base schema is always authoritative (baseAuthoritative: true). Pinned by the 3 CP-02 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S07-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Community node compatibility: accept canonical n8n declaration, compile, preserve supported fields, reject only invalid/unsafe, expose diagnostics, fallback only where required
checkpoints.purpose: Existing node definitions must work without mandatory rewrite (#223 §32). compileCommunityNodeDeclaration accepts a canonical n8n declaration, compiles it, preserves supported upstream fields, rejects ONLY truly invalid/unsafe forms (non-object, missing/invalid name), exposes compatibility diagnostics (warnings for unsupported fields, not rejections), and uses a fallback only where upstream semantics require it. P7 is an internal optimization + compatibility layer, NOT a new node-authoring language.
checkpoints.evidence: compileCommunityNodeDeclaration accepts a canonical n8n node declaration, compiles it, and preserves SUPPORTED_NODE_FIELDS; unsupported fields are downgraded to compatibility diagnostics (warnings, not rejections, preserved as opaque metadata); only truly invalid/unsafe forms (non-object, missing/invalid name) are rejected (NODE_DECLARATION_INVALID); fallbacks (type->name, parameters->{}, typeVersion->1) are applied only where upstream semantics require it, each with a reason. Pinned by the 4 CP-03 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S07-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Storage boundary: only bounded derived/cache state belongs in P7 (P7 does not become P8)

checkpoints.title: Differential oracle: compare P7 output against pinned n8n behavior and classify every difference
checkpoints.purpose: The differential oracle (#223 §40) compares P7 output against pinned n8n-workflow 2.9.1 behavior for the twelve aspects (visibility, defaults, options, dynamic options, dependent fields, resourceLocator, pagination, validation, error behavior, normalization, expression-dependent fields, credential-aware lookups) and classifies EVERY difference into one of the four closed classes: equivalent, compatible-improvement, migration-required, breaking. The comparison is canonical-JSON based with explicit superset/subset rules (a superset is a compatible improvement; dropping oracle data is breaking; a same-shape value change is migration-required). The oracle is an explicit, injectable, pinned reference — P7 never hardcodes vendor internals.
checkpoints.evidence: classifyDifference compares P7 output against the pinned n8n oracle for all 12 DIFFERENTIAL_ASPECTS (visibility, defaults, options, dynamic options, dependent fields, resourceLocator, pagination, validation, error behavior, normalization, expression-dependent fields, credential-aware lookups) and classifies every difference via a canonical-JSON superset/subset rule: equal -> EQUIVALENT, P7 a strict superset -> COMPATIBLE_IMPROVEMENT, P7 drops oracle data (subset) -> BREAKING, same shape different value -> MIGRATION_REQUIRED. The oracle is an explicit, injectable, pinned reference (P7 never hardcodes vendor internals). Pinned by the 5 CP-01 tests in test/lego-parameter-certify.test.mjs. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S08-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Certification report: a slice is certified only when no difference is breaking
checkpoints.purpose: certify() runs the differential cases and produces a frozen certification report { certified, total, differences, breaking }: certified is true ONLY when no difference is classified BREAKING (equivalent, compatible-improvement, and migration-required are tolerated, the latter with a migration note). The report is deterministic and the set of breaking differences is explicitly enumerated — a certification is a record, not a boolean hand-wave.
checkpoints.evidence: certify(cases) runs the differential cases and produces a frozen certification report { format, pinnedN8nVersion, certified, total, differences, breaking }: certified is true ONLY when no difference is classified BREAKING (equivalent/compatible-improvement/migration-required are tolerated), and the breaking set is explicitly enumerated. Malformed cases are rejected (CERTIFICATION_INVALID). Pinned by the 3 CP-02 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S08-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Negative/security test matrix: the 20 mandatory cases, each mapped to its expected marked failure or behavior
checkpoints.purpose: The mandatory negative/security matrix (#223 §41) is a frozen registry of the 20 required cases (cyclic dependency, invalid path, malformed/oversized provider response, excessive result count, timeout, cancellation, stale overlapping response, cache scope collision, wrong tenant, missing capability, provider without permission, credential access without P5, secret leakage through cache, secret leakage through logs, provider forged permission metadata, schema version mismatch, incompatible node definition, unbounded pagination, provider retry storm). verifyNegativeResult checks a P7 result is the expected marked failure code (or the expected no-leak/no-retry behavior) for each case, and runNegativeMatrix reports coverage + pass.
checkpoints.evidence: NEGATIVE_CASES is a frozen registry of all 20 mandatory negative/security cases (#223 §41: cyclic dependency, invalid path, malformed/oversized provider response, excessive result count, timeout, cancellation, stale overlapping response, cache scope collision, wrong tenant, missing capability, provider without permission, credential access without P5, secret leakage through cache/logs, provider forged permission metadata, schema version mismatch, incompatible node definition, unbounded pagination, provider retry storm); verifyNegativeResult checks each is the expected marked failure code (an unmarked empty success is explicitly NOT a pass) or the expected behavioral marker (no-leak/no-retry/forged-metadata); runNegativeMatrix reports coverage + pass, complete only when all 20 are covered and passing. Pinned by the 4 CP-03 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S08-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Low-resource budget: the 1 vCPU / 1 GB target (bounded cache, bounded concurrency, small pages, no persistent polling, bounded responses)
checkpoints.purpose: The low-resource target (#223 §38) is a frozen budget for 1 vCPU / 1 GB: amortized (compile-once) schema compilation, bounded cache, bounded provider concurrency, small pages/results, bounded/rejected large responses, and no persistent polling by default. checkLowResourceBudget verifies a config fits the budget and enumerates violations; P7 must degrade before it becomes a process-level memory pressure source. The performance strategy (#37) is honored: compile once, local graph, bounded cache, coalescing, lazy provider calls, cancellation, incremental recomputation — no network on static fields, no whole-form recomputation, no per-keystroke provider calls.
checkpoints.evidence: LOW_RESOURCE_BUDGET pins the 1 vCPU / 1 GB target (#223 §38): amortized (compile-once) schema compilation, no persistent polling, bounded cache (512 entries), bounded provider concurrency (8), small pages (200), bounded results (4096), bounded responses (1 MiB). checkLowResourceBudget verifies a config fits and enumerates violations (persistent polling, per-request compilation, unbounded cache/concurrency/pages/results/responses) — P7 degrades before it becomes a process-level memory pressure source. Pinned by the 2 CP-04 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S08-EVIDENCE.md.

checkpoints.title: Certification is a record: deterministic, reproducible, and tied to the pinned n8n version
checkpoints.purpose: The certification is a deterministic record pinned to n8n-workflow 2.9.1: re-running the same cases + oracle gives a byte-identical report (reproducibility), the pinned version is recorded, and a version change re-runs the matrix (a stale certification is invalid). This makes differential certification a repeatable gate, not a one-off assertion.

Pinned by the 2 CP-05 tests. See docs/n8n-lego/evidence/P7-S08-EVIDENCE.md.
